---
title: "With polars extension (.shz)"
toc: true
---

`shoez` ships an opt-in [polars](https://docs.pola.rs/) accessor for fitting
and applying steps in one expression, without building a `Recipe`. Importing
`shoez.polars` to register the `shz` accessor on polars DataFrames:

```{python}
import polars as pl
import polars.selectors as cs

import shoez.polars  # registers the `df.shz` accessor

orders = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "city": ["NYC", "LA", "NYC", "SF", "LA", "SF"],
        "price": [10.0, 20.0, None, 30.0, 25.0, 12.0],
        "qty": [2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 4],
    }
)

# drop any numeric columns with no variance
# TODO: fix PlExpr selection
#orders.shz.step_dummy(pl.col("city"))
```

Notice that `.step_dummy()` returned a new DataFrame with a column for each level in the `city` column.
In the following sections we'll show some of the more useful steps to use directly on a Polars DataFrame.


## Handle missing values: `step_impute_median`

`step_impute_median` fills nulls with the column's median (`step_impute_mean`
and `step_impute_mode` are the other flavors):

```{python}
#| eval: false
# TODO: pl.col() does not work here
filled = orders.shz.step_impute_median(pl.col("price"))
filled
```

## Multivariate feature engineering: `step_pca`

`step_pca` replaces numeric columns with their projection onto principal
components (here on the imputed frame, since PCA needs complete data):

```{python}
#| eval: false

# TODO: fix
(
    orders
    .shz.step_impute_median(pl.col("price"))
    .shz.step_pca(cs.numeric(), num_comp=2)
)
```
